forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Fylde expects Disabled Facilities Grants to underspend by about £400k against a £2.328m budget
news_drafts.lead:
Fylde Council expects to spend about £400k less than planned on Disabled Facilities Grants by the end of 2026/27, against a budget of £2.328m. The capital monitoring report to the Internal Affairs Scrutiny Committee says: "It is expected there will be an underspend at year end of approx £400k." Actual spending on the grants stood at £657k at 30 September 2026.

The report attributes the expected underspend to competitive contractor pricing and lower-value grants. The £2.328m budget includes £713k carried forward from 2025/26. The council's Better Care Fund grant for 2026/27 is £1.535m.

The committee also had the revenue budget monitoring report, position as at 30 September 2026. It says the council is repeating its annual budget rightsizing exercise in 2026/27. The exercise, which the paper says the council has run for several years, will "analyse underspends which have occurred over the last 3 financial years and to adjust current and future year budgets". The paper says the resulting changes will be reflected in the latest budgets and in the council's Financial Forecast.

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - APPENDIX A - P6 Capital Monitoring Report 2026.27
findings.headline: Garden Street, St Annes is contractually due for completion on 28 October 2026, with a latest budget of £1.295m and £656k spent to 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the scheme forms part of a linked programme with Pier Link and Orchard Road, and that it is expected to complete within budget. It does not report whether completion has taken place.
findings.matters: A contract completion date that falls before the meeting is a deadline the reader will want confirmed as met or missed.
findings.figures: £1.295m latest budget (£1,000k approved plus £295k slippage); £656k actual expenditure to 30 September 2026; £639k variance (FAV)
findings.quote: This project is contractually due for completion on the 28th October 2026

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - APPENDIX A - P6 Capital Monitoring Report 2026.27
findings.headline: Executive Committee approved a retrospective, fully funded addition of £86,284 to the capital programme for St Annes Promenade Paddling Pool remedial works.
findings.detail: The paper says the addition is funded from the Capital Investment Reserve and that the scheme is on target for completion in 2026/27. The addition was approved in September 2026.
findings.matters: A capital addition approved after the spend had started is a governance point, and it draws on the Capital Investment Reserve.
findings.figures: £86,284 retrospective addition; £86k latest budget; £76k actual expenditure to 30 September 2026
findings.quote: Executive Committee in Sept 26 approved a retrospective fully funded addition of £86,284 to the Council’s Capital Programme

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - APPENDIX A - P6 Capital Monitoring Report 2026.27
findings.headline: Disabled Facilities Grants are expected to underspend by approx £400k at year end, against a £2.328m budget.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the expected underspend to competitive contractor pricing and lower-value grants. It notes that the Better Care Fund grant for 2026/27 is £1.535m, and total budget includes £713k slipped from 2025/26.
findings.matters: An expected underspend on a grant-funded programme of this size indicates how much Better Care Fund money may be returned or carried over.
findings.figures: £2.328m total budget including £713k slippage; £657k actual expenditure to 30 September 2026; £1.535m Better Care Fund grant 2026/27; approx £400k expected year-end underspend
findings.quote: It is expected there will be an underspend at year end of approx £400k.

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - APPENDIX A - P6 Capital Monitoring Report 2026.27
findings.headline: St Annes Square Public Realm Improvements (Phase 1) was delivered under budget, with a committee report to follow on transferring the unspent £178k.
findings.detail: The paper says the scheme is contractually complete and in the defects period, with retention and professional fees still to be paid. It says a report will ask committee to approve transferring the unspent capital to the Pier Link and Garden Street schemes.
findings.matters: A scheme that completed with an underspend and a proposal to reallocate it is a reallocation decision other councils managing linked public realm projects may follow.
findings.quote: The scheme has been delivered under budget due to a number of identified risks not materialising.

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - APPENDIX A - P6 Capital Monitoring Report 2026.27
findings.headline: The Play Zones programme has £152k drawn down from the capital programme, and no construction start date has been confirmed.
findings.detail: The paper says three Play Zones are still at pre-construction stage, with the Rawstorne scheme progressing through design and planning. A £25k Lancashire Environmental Fund contribution supports Rawstorne, with £12.5k due in October 2026.
findings.matters: Funds have been committed to a programme that has not reached construction, and the paper says the Football Foundation timescales are still under review.
findings.figures: £152k drawdown from the Capital Programme; £18k increase in the council's contribution (April 2025 approval); £25k Lancashire Environmental Fund contribution
findings.quote: no construction start date has yet been confirmed.
